Yes, NovaLearn should fund the Advanced OCR work before accelerating Teams integration.

**Support demand**: Scanned PDFs are the primary driver of citation errors and onboarding delays [NL-001]. This has caused a "clogged" support queue, with 27% of May support tickets related to import issues and broken citations from scanned PDFs [NL-015]. This operational friction around scanned PDFs remains the primary onboarding bottleneck [NL-016-S01].

**Onboarding impact**: Scanned policy documents are the primary driver of customer onboarding delays [NL-001], and the OCR pipeline is a critical system stability requirement, not a nice-to-have [NL-015].

**Roadmap status**: The Advanced OCR Pipeline is scheduled for August 2026 and is the highest technical priority [NL-001]. The Teams integration is only "in design / planned for Q4 2026" and not generally available [NL-023]. In fact, the Teams connector is in a very early proof-of-concept phase, lacking security controls and tenant isolation [NL-023]. Rushing a Teams connector risks a tenant-isolation breach and requires a complete redesign of the auth layer [NL-015], and would just deliver inaccurate, un-cited answers to a larger audience [NL-015]. Consequently, OCR must remain the top priority for August, with Teams staying in design for Q4 and development slated for early 2027 [NL-015].
